intuition.title: Crystallite, particle and accessible surface are different quantities
intuition.text: The authors associate low BET area in low-water mixtures with sulfate-associated aggregation. Run3 has2.7nm Scherrer crystallites but about10nm TEM particles/aggregates; the reported particle-to-crystallite size ratio is3.7. This does not make the crystallites individually10nm. Runs4–7 surface-area estimates are described as comparable to crystallite size, suggesting single crystals; that is an interpretation, not atomic structural evidence.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied main pp.2–3, BET and TEM discussion

intuition.title: Water, alcohol and reflux time affect the reported outcomes
intuition.text: The authors propose that water and higher reflux temperatures favor hydrolysis, while adsorbed alcohol obstructs it. The table retains all individual outcomes, including the nonmonotonic low-water sizes. No unreported mixture boiling temperatures or continuous size predictor are supplied.
intuition.source_locator: Supplied main p.2, hydrolysis and solvent discussion

intuition.title: Surface cleaning depends on the treatment
intuition.text: Ammonia washing is associated with sulfate removal and higher surface area. Heating the ammonia-washed product at400°C for1h removes adsorbed ammonia; heating at600°C is associated with sulfate combustion and larger crystallites. The source does not establish that600°C material followed the ammonia/400°C sequence.

general_background.title: Condensation and return of solvent
general_background.summary: Reflux returns condensed vapour to a heated liquid and can limit net solvent loss. Condensation balances evaporation by returning solvent, while dissolved species continue to react in the liquid.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Recent Advances in the Liquid-Phase Syntheses of Inorganic Nanoparticles

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
